bullets.text: Lecture will cover meaning, importance, features, models, advantages, challenges, and applications of cloud computing.
Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services over the internet.
Services include servers, storage, databases, networking, software, analytics, and AI.
It's a way of renting computing resources instead of buying and maintaining them.
Analogy: Paying for electricity consumed, not owning the power plant.
Makes technology more affordable, scalable, and convenient.
On-demand self-service: Users access resources without human interaction.
Broad network access: Services available over the internet from various devices.
Features resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): Provider delivers fundamental computing resources (VMs, storage, networking).
Users build and manage their own applications; example: Amazon Web Services EC2.
Platform as a Service (PaaS): Provider delivers infrastructure plus a development platform with tools and databases.
Developers create applications without managing servers; example: Google App Engine.
Software as a Service (SaaS): Provider delivers ready-to-use applications over the internet.
Users access via a browser; examples: Gmail, Microsoft 365, Zoom.
Public cloud: Services delivered over the internet, shared by multiple organizations.
Cost-effective and scalable, but may raise security concerns.
Private cloud: Dedicated to a single organization, offering more control and security.
Hybrid cloud: Combines public and private clouds for flexibility and security.
Community cloud: Shared by several organizations with common goals (e.g., healthcare, education).

sections.heading: Advantages and Challenges of Cloud Computing

bullets.text: Advantages: Reduced costs, improved scalability, enhanced flexibility.
Advantages: Reliability (backup, disaster recovery), supports innovation.
Challenges: Security and privacy concerns for sensitive information.
Challenges: Downtime due to internet connectivity, compliance regulations.
Challenges: Vendor lock-in, performance concerns for high-speed applications.
Data storage and backup: Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive.
Business collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.
Entertainment: Netflix, Spotify streaming platforms.
Healthcare: Electronic medical records, telemedicine, AI-based diagnosis.
Education: Coursera, Google Classroom for online courses.
Research: Large-scale data analysis, machine learning, AI projects.
Cloud computing in AI and big data analytics: Renting high-performance computing resources for data processing.
Cloud providers offer machine learning services, natural language processing tools, and advanced analytics.
Edge computing: Data processed closer to the source (IoT devices) to reduce latency and support real-time decisions.
Edge computing still relies on the cloud for storage, management, and large-scale analysis.
Future trends: Multi-cloud strategies, serverless computing.
Future trends: Enhanced security and compliance, integration with AI, blockchain, and 5G.
